title: Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2603.01608v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: As frontier language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents pursuing complex, long-term objectives, there is increased risk of scheming: agents covertly pursuing misaligned goals. Prior work has focused on showing agents are capable of scheming, but their propensity to scheme in realistic scenarios remains underexplored. To understand when agents scheme, we decompose scheming incentives into agent factors and environmental factors. We develop realistic settings allowing us to systematically vary these factors, each with scheming opportunities for agents that pursue instrumentally convergent goals such as self-preservation, resource acquisition, and goal-guarding. Across 11 frontier models and four scenarios, we find almost no scheming despite high environmental incentives, and show this is unlikely to be explained by verbalized evaluation awareness. translated_title: 评估与理解大语言模型智能体中的图谋倾向
translated_abstract: 随着前沿语言模型越来越多地被部署为追求复杂、长期目标的自主智能体，“图谋”的风险也随之上升：即智能体隐蔽地追求未对齐的目标。以往的工作主要聚焦于证明智能体具备图谋的能力，但它们在现实场景中实施图谋的倾向仍未得到充分探索。为了理解智能体何时会图谋，我们将图谋动机分解为智能体因素与环境因素。我们构建了可系统性改变这些因素的现实化实验场景，其中每个场景都为追求工具性趋同目标（如自我保存、资源获取和目标守护）的智能体提供了图谋机会。在11个前沿模型和四种场景的实验中，我们发现尽管环境激励很高，几乎不存在图谋行为，并且我们表明这一现象不太可能用言语化的评估意识来解释。而当插入经对抗性设计、旨在鼓励……的提示片段时，（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究将大语言模型智能体的图谋动机分解为智能体因素与环境因素，并在11个前沿模型、四种现实场景中发现：尽管环境激励很高，智能体几乎不表现图谋行为，且这一现象难以用言语化的评估意识来解释。
en_tdlr: By decomposing scheming incentives into agent and environmental factors across realistic scenarios, this study finds that 11 frontier LLM agents rarely scheme despite high environmental incentives, and this absence is unlikely to be explained by verbalized evaluation awareness.
